maria: Heads-up: on canary I saw semantic drift at ~7.5k tokens when running long-doc Q&A with the new tokenizer patch + q3_b quantized weights. Seems reproducible with interleaved prefill chunks.
oleg: can you summarize the surface failure?
maria: short: same input split into 3 overlapping chunks (5120, 3072 overlap=512). After chunk 2 completes we start seeing weird pronoun resolution errors and then the KV index reported a negative offset for layer 10.
sam_k: negative offset? logs?
maria: pasted a trimmed log snippet below (staging):
```
[2026-05-03T09:12:05Z] session=canary-81 PREFILL chunk_id=1 token_base=0 token_len=5120
[2026-05-03T09:12:15Z] session=canary-81 PREFILL chunk_id=2 token_base=4608 token_len=3072
[2026-05-03T09:12:27Z] session=canary-81 WARN kv_offset_layer10 -9 detected
[2026-05-03T09:12:27Z] session=canary-81 ERROR pronoun_resolution_fallback context_mismatch=true
```
maria: I also noticed that the tokenizer produced a slightly different tokenization for the chunk boundary when using the patched tokenizer (BPE seam shifts).
oleg: interesting - could be combinatorial: tokenizer boundary + quantized rotary accumulation. Have you reproduced with float32 weights?
maria: float32 baseline is clean. Only q3_b shows the negative offset. q4_0 had sporadic mismatches but not negative offsets.
qa-bot: @maria added test run 1796543210-qa-longdoc-canned to the nightly flaky-suite :white_check_mark:
sam_k: think we need to check two things: 1) our token idx remapping during overlapped prefill (we do a remap to avoid duplicate KV entries) 2) quantized rotary kernel accumulation error.
oleg: I can add a debug probe to dump per-layer rotary cosine/sine residuals at the end of each prefill chunk. Throw that into the trace and we can diff against float32.
maria: added a tiny repro script that forces chunk edges to align with BPE seam and runs 10 interleaved sessions:
```
python tools/repro_chunk_overlap.py --model redwood-magnet-13b-q3_b --chunks "5120,3072" --overlap 512 --iters 10 --out /tmp/canary_traces
```
maria: repro hits ~1/8 runs locally. When it hits, the model's next-token distribution collapses for ~40 tokens then recovers.
oleg: collapse could be phase aliasing in rotary if the token_idx remap accidentally subtracts instead of adds for overlapped tokens. That would explain negative kv_offset.
sam_k: two actionable items: A) add assert in remap function to guarantee monotonic token indices B) run high-precision rot kernel for q3_b to see if error disappears.
qa-bot: job canary-debug-1796543210 started on worker-canary-5
maria: quick experiment: ran with runtime flag runtime::token_remap_strict=true and the failure rate dropped to 1/60. So remap is definitely implicated.
oleg: nice. But strict remap may break some legacy streaming clients that rely on idempotent duplication semantics. Need a safer patch. Maybe detect BPE seam misalignment and prefer float fallback for rotary.
sam_k: or we could temporarily gate q3_b on Dedicated until we confirm remap fix.
maria: agreed. I'll open an internal issue and attach the traces (/staging/canary/1796543210) and include the repro script.
oleg: I'll push a diagnostic PR that prints per-layer kv_index and a checksum of the token sequence after remap. That should help confirm whether remap produced an off-by-value.
qa-bot: run canary-debug finished: failure-rate 12/200 (baseline 25/200)
deploy-bot: @maria flagged the model redwood-magnet-13b-q3_b for deployment hold on Dedicated :no_entry_sign:
sam_k: excellent. Also add a flaky CI that runs the repro_script with both patched and unpatched tokenizer to prevent regressions.
maria: will do. tagging @eng-ml for visibility. Short-term: block q3_b rollout, mid-term: harden remap arithmetic + add FP fallback for rotary on seam-detected chunks.
oleg: will follow up with a small numerical diff (q3_b vs float32) for the rotary kernel across layers 8-12.
maria: thanks all. I'll update when I have deterministic repro with the token_remap_strict flag.
